protocol.research_question: Does explicitly providing pair novelty improve AML prediction when counts and both port ranks are retained, under a shared validation-governed training protocol?
protocol.design_history: Prospective follow-up to inspected five-epoch results on the same HI-Small graph; not a previously untouched test set or cross-dataset replication. User requested a separate8-hour allocation budget before this protocol was run; do not pool with the25-run protocol.

data.tie_order: timestamp then fixed label-independent permutation from NumPy default_rng(0)
data.novelty_definition: first observed directed sender-receiver pair within this dataset history

model.architecture: original two-layer GIN, fixed reference hyperparameters

preprocessing.apply: one frozen affine transform across all splits and arms
preprocessing.shared_pair_fit: pool training values of the distinct-count and corresponding port columns with equal weight; sample standard deviation (ddof=1)
preprocessing.other_columns: independent training mean and sample standard deviation; zero scale replaced by one
preprocessing.invariant: Both raw and float32 normalized distinct-count/port equalities must reproduce novelty on every edge
preprocessing.interpretation: Novelty is a linearly separable deterministic predicate in counts+ports, not new information or increased theoretical expressivity.

training.selection: exact maximum validation AP; earliest tie
training.stopping: After at least20 epochs, stop after10 stale epochs under the same0.001 validation AP rule, or at30.
training.threshold: maximum validation F1 at selected checkpoint; first argmax
training.test_access: deferred until individual run training complete
training.evaluation: model.eval, fixed seed-specific split sampling, restore training RNG
training.epoch_randomness: reseed independently by seed block and epoch

analysis.strong_support_rule: primary F1 and corroborating AP paired 95% intervals both strictly above zero; otherwise report narrower or inconclusive evidence
analysis.uncertainty: Paired Student t95, n5/df4 for all contrasts; fixed-data training variation only; secondary unadjusted.
analysis.cap_rule: report capped/unplateaued runs; no automatic convergence claim
analysis.no_adaptation: no outcome-driven groups, seeds, budget extensions, or endpoint switching

power.test: two-sided paired t with noncentral-t power
power.planning_source: Pilot CN-CP (replacement), not observed B-A variance; different protocol
power.interpretation: Planning sensitivity, not guaranteed power or business materiality; primary F1 test only, not joint F1/AP success; no outcome-driven seed extensions. This budget revision uses5 seeds, so the planning detectable primary F1 difference is5.00 points, not2.96.

analysis.robustness_rule: Separate descriptive within-benchmark robustness flag: primary F1 and AP intervals positive, and B-A F1/AP point contrasts positive for days8-9 at primary checkpoint, fixed epoch20, and final checkpoint. No endpoint switching; no convergence or cross-dataset claim.

execution.gpu_model: four identical GPUs; HKU template RTX3090
execution.failure_policy: Any failed or truncated run makes the batch incomplete; all15 are required; retain epoch checkpoints.
execution.budget_note: Queueing is excluded; full completion within8 hours is conditional on GPU allocation and measured throughput. No outcome-driven budget adaptation.

probe.interpretation: Exploratory linear decodability only; cannot establish causal model use or prove absence of nonlinear encoding.
probe.fit: training features and labels only; train-fitted StandardScaler; representative random subsets without balancing
probe.threshold: fixed 0.5 plus threshold maximizing balanced accuracy on validation only

conclusion.statement: The primary F1 interval includes zero; the experiment does not establish a positive addition effect or equivalence.
conclusion.rule: The broad prediction claim requires positive 95% intervals for both primary F1 and corroborating AP.
conclusion.mechanism: No outcome identifies failure to infer novelty inside the model; input effects are not a causal decomposition of internal computation.

within_benchmark_robustness.rule: Primary F1/AP intervals positive, and F1/AP point contrasts positive on days 8–9, fixed epoch 20 and final epoch.
within_benchmark_robustness.interpretation: Sensitivity directions are descriptive, reuse the same data, and do not establish convergence, cross-dataset generalization or additional multiplicity-controlled discoveries.
